# WTS source excerpts

Captured from public When To Stream pages on 13–14 November 2026. `manifest.json` records original URLs, subjects and capture timestamps. HTML retains canonical links, headings, credits and release fields; scripts, styles and unrelated recommendations are omitted. The newer excerpts contain only the original native subject paragraphs. RSS retains one original item with its CDATA and namespaces. These are parser regression fixtures, not current release data.

The first three manifest profiles are permanent live anchors. Each daily probe also checks two rotating profiles from the remaining international, documentary and multi-platform subjects, plus the RSS feed. Network concurrency is capped at two; a failed check gets one retry. Confirmed failures fail the workflow. JSONL evidence is retained for thirty days and the workflow summary distinguishes recovered checks, missing fields, malformed fields and transport failures. No credentials, database writes or messages are involved.

`regressions` records genuine upstream malformed content excluded from the healthy live canary set: EPIC has the truncated PVOD year `202`. Its valid subscription date survives; the invalid rental date is never inferred. Project Hail Mary's two clearly labelled subscription platform premieres exercise earliest-availability selection with the corresponding platform. Same-platform conflicts, incomplete segments and unknown platforms remain withheld.

Investigate failures before replacing snapshots or changing parser rules. Legitimate date changes are allowed; native identity, field presence and valid date structure remain required.
